linguistic_propositions.proposition: A coordinated element carries the same case as the element it is joined to, whichever of the six connectors is used.
The plain additive connector asserts no ordering between the two elements it joins.
One connector marks sequence with no interval and another marks sequence with an interval; the choice is fixed by the real-world interval, not by anything in the string.
The correction connector cancels a preceding negated element and affirms what follows it, while after an affirmed element it upgrades rather than cancels.
The adversative connector contrasts the two elements without cancelling the first.
When the adversative connector carries an attached pronoun it is no longer a coordinator but the doubled abrogator of the إنّ family.
The six items presented exhaust the coordinator inventory.
Each of the six items functions only as a coordinator.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: Operator choice is fixed by time reference and clause type; no single negator serves all cases.
The past-negating particle takes an imperfect verb in the jussive; the future-negating particle takes an imperfect verb in the subjunctive.
The general negator leaves the indicative untouched in ongoing-action negation but takes a jussive in the prohibitive use.

ليس belongs to the كان family, taking a nominative subject and an accusative predicate.
ليس has no imperfect and no imperative; its perfect shape carries present-time meaning.

The general negator followed by an indefinite noun without tanwin negates the whole class rather than an instance.
ليس never precedes a verb.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The jussive after the past-negating particle is realised as sukun on a sound final, deletion of a final weak letter, deletion of a medial weak letter, or deletion of the final nun of the five forms.
The subjunctive after the future-negating particle is realised as fatha on a sound final, fatha on or estimated over a weak final, retention of the medial weak letter, or deletion of the final nun.
The medial weak letter is deleted only in the jussive, so its presence or absence discriminates the two moods for hollow verbs.
For the five forms the two moods are formally identical, so mood is recoverable only from the particle or from context.
The verb's shape does not determine its time reference; the particle does.
A defective verb ending in a long alif shows no change at all in the subjunctive.
One doubled-verb jussive form in the material is explained as a contraction of a plural form conditioned by a following plural subject.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The relative pronoun agrees with its antecedent in gender and number but never in case.
The singular and masculine-plural forms are built and never change shape; only the dual forms alternate between a nominative and an oblique shape.
A non-human plural antecedent takes the feminine-singular form.
A relative pronoun is licensed only by a definite antecedent; an indefinite antecedent takes the clause directly with no relative pronoun.
Definiteness conferred by إضافة to a definite noun licenses the relative pronoun exactly as the article does, as do proper nouns and pronouns.
The clause following the relative pronoun must be a complete predication: verbal, nominal, or a self-sufficient prepositional predicate.
A returning pronoun linking the clause back to the antecedent must always be present, either overt or hidden.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The returning pronoun's case is fixed by its role inside the clause and is independent of the antecedent's case.
The returning pronoun agrees with the antecedent in gender and number.
When the antecedent corresponds to the clause's subject, the returning pronoun is a hidden pronoun inside the verb.
In a passive clause the hidden returning pronoun is the deputy subject.
The returning pronoun may be deleted only when it is an accusative direct object of the clause verb and no ambiguity results.
Deletion of a preposition-governed returning pronoun, or of a possessor, is never licensed.
A prepositional phrase containing the returning pronoun can itself serve as the clause's predicate.
The clause must be a complete sentence.
